target: Crowd annotators' binary judgement of stress expressed in Reddit text

source.citation: Turcan and McKeown (2019). Dreaddit: A Reddit Dataset for Stress Analysis in Social Media. LOuHI, pp. 97–107.
source.licensing_note: Downloaded from the authors' public research release. The ZIP contains no separate dataset license; do not assume that the app's code license covers Reddit data or model redistribution.

training.features: TF-IDF words and word bigrams, min_df=2, max_features=30000, sublinear_tf=True; no metadata
training.tuning: No hyperparameter search or test-set tuning performed.

evaluation.split: Authors' supplied test split, retained unchanged; overlapping posts/text removed from training
evaluation.scope: Metrics describe this text classifier on this dataset, before app input guards; they do not validate face cues or multimodal stress estimation.

limitations: Crowd labels describe perceived stress in text; they are not clinical or self-reported stress measurements.
English Reddit narratives differ from short personal check-ins, other languages and everyday conversation.
Exact normalized text and post-ID overlap is removed from training; near-duplicate wording and shared authors cannot be ruled out (no author identifier supplied).
Several test segments can come from one post, so rows are not fully independent.
The model can learn topic and subreddit associations; no subgroup fairness or external validation has been performed.
TF-IDF may misread negation, sarcasm, quoted speech and context. Term contributions are associations, not causes.
predict_proba scores are uncalibrated model outputs, not probabilities that a person is stressed.
No separate validation set, calibration, uncertainty interval or cross-domain test was used.
